title: bug: the daemon reads .moe/daemon.json with no size cap (readDaemonInfo, doctor probe)
description:
Objective: bound the daemon's own reads of .moe/daemon.json. Two readers call fs.readFileSync on the whole file:
- packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts readDaemonInfo, used by start's lock check, status and stop;
- src/commands/doctor.ts probeDaemonJson.
This is a sibling of task-4f1e37f30ee548298b26e17c0b6ea84e (the JetBrains reader, same cap). daemon.json is repository content: a repository can commit one past .moe/.gitignore. A huge or never-ending file (a symlink to /dev/zero) therefore makes start, status, stop and doctor allocate up to gigabytes before they fail.

Deliverable:
- Both readers go through one bounded read of at most 65537 bytes. The cap is 64 KiB (65536 bytes), the JetBrains value.
- A file over the cap is handled exactly like an unparseable one: readDaemonInfo returns null, and doctor reports a fail that names the 64 KiB limit and echoes no file content.
- Read through a file descriptor, never a whole-file read, and never a size pre-check alone: a symlink to a device reports size 0.
- No deletion for size alone. Valid files behave as today.

Not in scope:
- the daemon.json write path and format;
- benchmarks/baselineRun.ts, which reads its own temp project;
- the other clients (proxy, Claude Code plugin, VS Code, launchers, JetBrains), which have their own sibling tasks.

Verification: cd packages/moe-daemon && npx tsc --noEmit && npm test. On WSL the shared checkout's node_modules is a Windows install, so run it from a Linux snapshot (Serena mem gotcha-daemon-linux-snapshot-gate).
definitionOfDone: index.ts readDaemonInfo returns the parsed info for a valid daemon.json of exactly 65536 bytes (JSON padded with spaces) and null for one of 65537 bytes, proven by new vitest cases.

doctor's daemon.json probe reports a fail that names the 64 KiB limit for a 65537-byte file and echoes none of its content, and still passes a valid 65536-byte file, proven by new doctor.test.ts cases.
Neither reader loads more than 65537 bytes of daemon.json, proven by a test (for example, readFileSync is never called on daemon.json, or a sparse multi-GiB file is refused promptly).
Fresh cd packages/moe-daemon && npx tsc --noEmit && npm test exits 0.
